text:
New York spent the first two periods making a 2% chance look like an omen. Sean Durzi's snap shot 1:18 into the game, a look that scores about one time in fifty, put the Rangers ahead, and by the time the second period ended Anaheim was down 4-0 without having scored a goal of its own.

The shooting was kind to New York, but the play was not far behind the score. The Rangers produced 4.47 expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances, not just their number) to Anaheim's 3.29, and in simulated replays of every shot they win 68% of the time. Their second period did the damage. J.T. Miller tipped in a power-play goal, Gabe Perreault and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on 34% and 27% chances, and Bjorkstrand added another early in the third. Anaheim actually had more shot attempts, 62 to 55, and Tim Washe had a 34% look stopped by Dylan Garand.

Garand deserved the credit for keeping the shutout alive that long. He saved about 1.3 goals more than the quality of the shots against him would predict, while Ville Husso allowed five on 4.47 expected goals. Nick Jensen and A.J. Greer scored 36 seconds apart late in the third, at 18:51 and 19:27, but the deficit was too large by then. Bjorkstrand, with two goals, took first star.
